I wanted to like this game, I love these kinds of games, but I gotta advise against it.

To start, there's only 3 classes. That is just way too small of a pool for what this kind of game is trying to be, and one class is locked behind game progress. Ninja and Soldier just don't appeal much to me, I would've liked some sort of mage or paladin class (made to fit into the game's world obviously).

Beyond that, it feels like a slog to get through. I know one review said to just keep at it, but it doesn't feel very rewarding at the start of the game, unlike other roguelites that usually boost you up with meta upgrades [i]just[/i] enough to feel like you're getting somewhere. It's small, but that little boost makes losing the next run feel much less crushing. I took a damage boost, but I was doing enough damage regardless, and my struggle seemed more like staying alive. Heals are few and far between and I felt pretty on edge needing to play perfectly to progress farther.

That coupled with another review that said all nanite upgrades and weapons are reset upon advancing to the next difficulty, that's just soul crushing. I don't want to get all that way and then have to upgrade all of that [i]again[/i].

These are just personal gripes, though, and if this game sounds appealing to you regardless I would say go for it. But for people like me, I'm afraid it's a pass.

[h1]Roguelite:[/h1]
5/10

Runs aren't really that much different from one another. Guns drop all over the place and in multiple runs to the very last area, I've seen close to at least every single weapon dropping once.

Now here's the issue: Weapons don't get better as you progress. The SMG that drops in the last area has the same stats as the starting one. It has a different synergy (bonus for having a specific upgrade), but the stats are the same. So you can always make your favorite build every run.

Drops are also a bit boring. Once your gun's modded, that's it. That's your weapon for the rest of the run. Guns and mods need slightly randomized stats and to get stronger as you progress through the floors. Make me excited to get loot, compare, and play different runs based on what I got.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]
8/10

This is, for me, the saving grace. It's really fun when you get into a flow and the intensity of enemies and how you need to play differently does increase in a straight line.

It loses points because the differences in difficulty between characters is completely bonkers. Ninja's right click is an instant de-aggro. It's the best ability in the game, bar none. It carries runs. There's absolutely no point in playing the Soldier, ever. Hacker's okay. Requires more effort but can achieve a lot more than the other 2.

You got Dodge, double jump (upgrade), reload while sprinting and doing other things. It's a good medium-fast pace. You really gotta work your brain as far as kill priority for some rooms in some areas if you're not Ninja.

[h1]Soundtrack:[/h1]
5/10

Nothing to write home about but it's okay for what it is. Not enough variety in my opinion. I can imagine that if you're struggling a bit and stuck in the first level, that one song's really gonna start getting annoying.

[h1]Before you refund:[/h1]
Try and get further. Look at the nanite upgrades. For some reason, they put all of what's typically unlocked with progression, very very CORE gameplay features in Nanite upgrades. Secondary weapon, Heavy weapon, Ultimate, Weapon mod slots, these are all things that you'll need either to become strong enough, or to actually use what the game drops for you (have fun). These all require dropping 1 point in their own Nanite upgrade, which are all mixed in with the other ones. Prioritize those, get them and see if the game's better afterwards. It totally went from Mediocre to Pretty Good for me, after getting these.

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
It's fun, but I'm a gameplay kind of person, so the negatives don't impact me that much. I don't really see myself grinding this to no end like many other roguelites, however. Since I can always make the build I want, and some things are just way too good. If I want to finish the game, I know just how to do it! 

It just gets boring after a while, as I prefer to leave my fate in the Roguelite's carefully balanced RNG, usually. Make ME adapt to the game. Throw me curveballs so that I feel like I'm constantly improving rather than merely grinding. That's what Roguelites should be about. Unfortunately, after a few runs, it feels a lot more like a grind than a series of fun surprises.

If you are a FPS roguelike fan who are looking for another game to sink in some hours, I would not recommend this game. This game feels like a cheap flash game copy of Returnal and Deadlink. Movement, player animations (weapon swapping and shooting), enemy attack indication/sound effect, mini-map, and character abilities all feel clunky.

The game plays mostly like Returnal in a cyberpunk setting. You get a gun with weapon mods (synergizes with skills you get which half the time you don't get the skill for) that doesn't really change your run to feel unique. Bullet projectile speed is way too slow for mid/long range shots, and some guns just feel wrong (the sniper). You get upgrades in the run like artifact, but it is randomized and once you commit that is what you are committing to upgrade. To be honest, the game would have more success just being a turn-off your brain hoard-shooter than a roguelike. 

Progression in this game, via nanites, is much like Gunfire's soul-essence. You gain nanites by clearning levels or opening chests, but it is executed poorly. First damage upgrade straight up increases damage by 15% up to 150%. Everything that will help you progress the game and enjoy the roguelike mechanics of the game is blocked by 'grinding'. You don't even get to use the 'ultimate ability' until you unlock it. First few games just feel like BS, because if you had nanites, the game would be super easy anyways with your stats being almost all doubled. It just gate keeps harder difficulty and adds padding time.

Animations for everything feels sluggish. Dash feels lifeless, swapping between melee to shooting is slow, abilities only add another layer of clunkiness. For being a ninja robot in a cyberpunk settings, it just feels wrong to feel this bad to play. Game visibility/readability is another problem. Mini-map looks cool but half the time, I cannot tell what is an enemy and a weapon drop at a glance. I cannot even understand which direction in going to when traversing the map since the map design is so repetitive. 

It's a cool concept and design, but it just isn't that good of a game. The core mechanics just feel to wrong in many ways. If things get smoothed out more to feel more fluid, the game would be decently fun. Oh, they also made Die After Sunset, no wonder everything feels clunky. I guess there are some improvements.

Edit: 5/2/23:
This is one who's future is bright as the very first patch addressed nearly every single point of contention in the community.

Very challenging, fights require you to be precise in movement and aiming. Upgrades are effective but don't cater to a broken playstyle, much more geared towards giving you more options in combat based upon your situational awareness. Each weapon has it's purpose and can be buffed really only by one aspect (Weapons have an affinity towards one of your four major upgrade slots) which at first was strange, but when you find a weapon you like to use have the affinity of an upgrade you are currently building it feels /really/ good. Aesthetically the game is gorgeous, and blends together well with it's soundtrack and sound effects. 

Pros:
- Almost entirely skill based. Upgrades are there to enhance options, mostly requiring skill to use any given upgrade effectively.

- Pacing is slow, methodical and cerebral. Everything you do is simple, does a single thing and does it well enough that you are almost required to use every last bit to your advantage, as if you don't you almost certainly will die very quickly.

- Enemy design is extremely simple, easy to read and gives a "combat chess" feeling when it comes to approaching larger fights.

- No silly rock-paper-scissors element system, to my knowledge the only status effect I've seen thus far is stun which is frankly, all this game needs in order to keep combat as strong as it is.

-Music, atmosphere and sound effects are pleasing, nothing stands out particularly but overall the presentation is great.

-Risk/reward is baked right into combat at almost every decision. Being good at this game seemingly requires you to make risky decisions that could end a run or clear an encounter without taking damage. Anything in between probably means you're going to die in the next room unless you go into it with a plan.

Neutral/Cons:

- Level design (At least in first "biome") is extremely bland and repetitive, understandable as knowing the layout of a level gives a very large advantage to approaching your combat options. Just needs 3-4 more layouts/rooms to make each run feel unique, as right now you're going to see the same 5(?) rooms linked together.

-While upgrades are very impactful and skill based, they are pretty slim pickings, but what is there allows you to genuinely make your own playstyle for your character.

-Jump animation / feel is poopie please make it a little bit more lively or something. Collision is also slightly wonky.

tl;dr
8/10
needs more of what is there, but understandable to why it is currently slim as the balance of upgrades vs game knowledge vs skill/decision making is phenominal
